rationale: Evidence: the baseline (iteration 0) never finished on any development track. Every trial ended off track, with progress only 0.10 to 0.15, max_error about 0.06 m (the off-track limit), and one line-loss event per run. The robot is losing the line early, not slowly drifting. Likely causes: (1) at base_speed 1.6 with a 0.04 m sensor look-ahead, the correction arrives late, so the robot overshoots each bend; (2) kd 0.1 gives too little damping against that overshoot; (3) the body is heavier than needed for quick turn response. Changes: base_speed 1.6 to 1.4, which trades some speed for stability while keeping a path to about 1.4 m/s. kp 2.0 to 3.0 for a stronger correction at the bend edges. kd 0.1 to 0.4 to damp the overshoot. ki 0.05 to 0.02 to limit integral windup on bends. Sensor look-ahead y 0.04 to 0.03 to cut the reaction lag. Mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg to speed up turn response. Geometry otherwise unchanged (5 sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03, 12 mm footprint, weights -2 to 2, last_direction line loss). Expected result: fewer off-track exits and progress above 0.5 on the oval and s-bend. Hypotheses to check: if max_error still reaches 0.06 on the s-bend, the cause is turn overshoot and kd should rise further; if progress stalls on the slalom, kp is too high. Measurements wanted next: progress, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, completion_time, and control_effort.
